_comment: GENERATED BY MATUGEN - do not edit by hand. Template: ~/.config/matugen/templates/quickshell-colors.json
_policy: Two axes, and they are the same two every other application in this setup follows: SURFACES, TEXT and OUTLINES come from the scheme (the ui_* roles, fixed for as long as the scheme is) and ACCENTS come from the wallpaper (the Material 3 roles, regenerated on every change). The shell used to be the one exception -- its surfaces followed the image as well -- and the header of Theme.qml still argues for that exception. The argument was sound while the alternative was a base fixed at Tokyo Night forever: M3 guarantees the contrast of each role PAIR whatever the wallpaper is, which was worth more than a base nobody could change. It is not worth more than the base the user picked. desktop-scheme moves the background of GTK, Qt, kitty and zathura and used to leave the shell's alone, so choosing a scheme changed the whole desktop except the part of it this repository draws. The pairing rule itself still holds and still matters -- on_surface over surface, on_primary over primary, never a hardcoded hex over a generated one -- but on this side of the fence the pairs are the scheme's, and a scheme is contrast-checked once, by hand, when it is written, instead of per wallpaper by M3.
_surface_ladder: THE LADDER IS NO LONGER A RULE IN THIS FILE. It used to be: `surface` was the window and the three containers climbed the raised tones, ui_bg -> ui_bg_raised -> ui_bevel_midlight -> ui_border, one global mapping for every scheme. That rule was reasoned for and the reasoning was half right -- all three schemes really do have four separable tones ABOVE their window while below it Tokyo Night has five steps, Catppuccin three and Gruvbox two, so climbing was the only mapping that never spent two M3 levels on one hex. What it got wrong is that it read Qt bevel slots as if they were an elevation scale and then imposed Gruvbox's answer on the other two. Under Tokyo Night it painted the shell in tones Tokyo Night does not use for surfaces at all: ui_bevel_midlight #353b55 is not upstream at all -- it is a Util.blend this repository computed to fill QPalette::Midlight (schemes/README.md 4.1(c)) -- and ui_border #414868 is `terminal_black`, which upstream assigns to ANSI bright black and to dimmed foreground text and to no surface anywhere. So the shell rendered greys where Tokyo Night renders blacks. Now each scheme names its own four: ui_surface, ui_surface_container, ui_surface_container_high, ui_surface_container_highest, documented in schemes/README.md 1.1 and derived per scheme from that project's own published UI ports -- see 4.4 there for the citations, tone by tone. WHAT EVERY SCHEME STILL AGREES ON IS THE DIRECTION, and it is not a matter of taste: levels 3 and 4 are where this shell paints HOVER. Of the 46 sites reading surface_container_high, 33 are a hover or focus fill and 23 of those are literally `containsMouse ? level : "transparent"`; of the 25 reading surface_container_highest, 9 are hover fills and the other 16 are tooltips, rails, meters, chips and field fills. Those totals were counted before the shared components were split across the theme seam and the tree now reads 44 and 24; the classification behind them was done by hand, site by site, and has not been re-done, so take the proportion rather than the number -- what it is evidence for is the direction, and nothing that moved changed a hover into a recess. A ladder that descended would turn every hover in the tree into a recess, and all three projects put their own hover ABOVE their ground anyway -- Tokyo Night's CursorLine bg_highlight, Catppuccin's list.hoverBackground surface0, Gruvbox's CursorLine bg1. So all three ladders climb. WHAT THEY DISAGREE ON IS WHERE THEY START, which is the datum that could never be expressed before: Tokyo Night and Catppuccin both publish chrome BELOW their content ground (bg_dark and black under bg; crust and mantle under base) so both ladders begin on the palette floor and the shell's panels go near-black, while Gruvbox publishes nothing under bg0 at all -- bg0_h and bg0_s are alternative VALUES for bg0 selected by g:gruvbox_contrast_dark, never a second surface -- so Gruvbox begins at its window and does not move. Gruvbox is the scheme the old rule happened to fit. MEASURE THE STEPS IN L*, NOT IN CONTRAST RATIO: at this end of the scale the ratio compresses badly, and the old ladder's narrowest rung was 5.8 L* (1.22:1) while Tokyo Night's new narrowest is 5.7 L* (1.13:1) -- the same step to an eye, two very different-looking numbers. Nothing collapses in any scheme; the closest any two levels come is Tokyo Night's 5.7 L*.
_outlines: The two outline roles stay outside the ladder, and now that each scheme names its own four surfaces they can be checked against it rather than argued around it. `outline` takes ui_text_muted, which sits above every surface level in all three schemes -- and which is what the shell actually paints with it: Theme.outline is a TEXT colour far more often than a border (the placeholder in SearchField.qml, a muted line in AudioPage.qml, an undescribed bind in KeybindsPage.qml), and 'placeholder text, present but not readable as content' is ui_text_muted's definition word for word. `outline_variant` takes ui_border_dim, a divider, which is what it is drawn as everywhere. THE COLLISION THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO RECORD IS DOWN FROM TWO SCHEMES TO ONE. It was that ui_border_dim and ui_bevel_midlight are one tone in both Catppuccin and Gruvbox, so an outline_variant border on surface_container_high melted into its own fill at themes/genesis/components/SettingsSection.qml:110 and modules/settings/pages/UpdatesPage.qml:398. Catppuccin's ladder no longer contains surface1 #45475a, so under Catppuccin those two borders now stand at 1.38:1 instead of 1.00:1. Gruvbox is unchanged and still collides there -- bg2 #504945 is both its ui_border_dim and its third surface -- and the mitigation is the one that always applied: in both sites the fill is the HOVER state of a pill that is transparent at rest, so the pill reads against the card behind it. Tokyo Night never collided and improves anyway, 1.12:1 -> 1.37:1 on surface_container_high and 1.10:1 -> 1.14:1 on surface_container_highest, because its ladder no longer tops out one step from fg_gutter. THE CONSTRAINT THIS PUT ON THE LADDER IS WORTH KEEPING VISIBLE: surface_container_highest is the ground under seven outline_variant borders including every tooltip (themes/genesis/components/Tooltip.qml:46 fills with it and borders with outline_variant at :48), so a scheme must not spend its ui_border_dim tone on level 4. That is why Catppuccin's level 4 is surface2 and not surface1, and why Tokyo Night's is #343a55 and not fg_gutter #3b4261.
_alerts: ON THIS SIDE OF THE FENCE, and the distinction is the whole point. An alert must not follow the WALLPAPER: amber is 'watch out' and red is 'something is wrong' whatever image is on screen, and M3's error role is derived from the image, so over a red picture a critical reading would come out the hue of the rest of the bar. That argument is untouched -- see `_no_error_role` below, which is why this file still passes no error/on_error through. What it never meant is 'hardcoded'. A scheme is not a wallpaper: it is chosen by hand and it moves only when the user moves it, so an alert taken from a scheme is as fixed as anything on screen is. GTK, Qt and zathura have painted their alerts from sem_* since the templates were substituted; the shell was the last surface on the desktop still showing Tokyo Night amber and red on a Gruvbox base, and these three keys are what ends that. MEASURED UNDER ALL THREE SCHEMES against all four surface levels, and it is not all one way: warning improves everywhere (worst pair 3.26 -> 3.84 on Gruvbox, 3.34 -> 5.25 on Catppuccin), Tokyo Night does not move because the literals were its scheme, and Gruvbox's critical gets WORSE -- #fb4934 is darker than #f7768e, so on surface_container_highest (#665c54, Gruvbox's own bg3) it falls 2.46:1 to 1.89:1. The weak pairing is Gruvbox's red on Gruvbox's bg3, it is weak in every application here and not only in the shell, and it is fixed in schemes/gruvbox-dark.json if it is worth fixing. The long version is in Theme.qml, where the readers are.
_alerts_not_emitted: sem_on_warning and sem_success are filled by every scheme and are deliberately NOT here, for the reason `_no_error_role` records: a key nothing reads is a colour written into the void. THERE IS NO textOnWarning BECAUSE THERE IS NOWHERE TO PAINT IT. All 24 sites that touch Theme.warning were classified -- 24 was the census when this was written, the tree reads 34 today, and they have not been re-classified -- and every one of the 24 is a foreground -- a Text, a Nerd Font glyph, a border, a meter tick, a slider fill with nothing on it -- or a Qt.alpha() tint of 0.16 to 0.22 over a card, and on none of those four tints does anything switch to an on-warning ink -- what sits on them is either textOnSurface or the amber itself. Not one solid amber ground in the tree carries readable content. Theme.textOnCritical, by contrast, has real sites, all the same shape: hovering a Forget button fills it solid red and flips the glyph. There are three of them today -- modules/settings/pages/NetworkPage.qml:524, modules/settings/pages/BluetoothPage.qml:548, themes/genesis/island/Island.qml:952 -- where this paragraph said four and named these same three. It would also be a duplicate key: sem_on_warning and sem_on_critical are the same hex in all three schemes. AND THERE IS NO success BECAUSE THE SHELL HAS NO 'IT WORKED' COLOUR AT ALL: no green hex exists anywhere in the QML tree, and the states that would want one -- an `ok` update verdict, a connected network, a paired device, a charging battery -- are painted Theme.primary today. Giving them a green is a design change with its own argument to make, and it has to happen on the drawing side first; this key would follow it, not lead it. Both roles stay in the vocabulary because GTK consumes them. Add either key here on the day a reader appears in Theme.qml, in the same change.
_accents: Below this line nothing changed and nothing should: these nine are the wallpaper's half of the desktop, derived by matugen from the image on every change, and they are why Theme.qml reads this file through a watching FileView instead of being generated as QML. They keep their M3 pairing among themselves -- on_primary is only ever painted on primary, on_primary_container only on primary_container -- because that pairing is the only contrast guarantee an accent has.
_no_error_role: M3 has error/on_error and this file used to emit them, and Theme.qml read neither: it held `warning` and `critical` as literals instead, because an alert tinted by the wallpaper loses the one thing it is for. So the two lines wrote a colour nothing could consume, and they went. The alerts have a source now -- the scheme's sem_* roles, above -- and it is still not this one: error/on_error stay out because they are derived per image, which is the fault, not because the shell has nothing to paint red with. THE RULE THE PARAGRAPH IS REALLY FOR is the one that outlived its example: every key in this file is read by exactly one property in Theme.qml, and every such property reads a key. Keep it that way. If some role really is wanted, add the reader in the same change.
